questions.stem_text:
What is the primary lipoprotein secreted from the liver that is at least partially
composed of dietary derived lipids?
questions.answer_explanation: VLDL, or very-low-density lipoprotein, is the primary lipoprotein secreted by the liver that transports triglycerides, which are often derived from dietary fats, to peripheral tissues for energy utilization and storage.

questions.stem_text: The patellar tap is a clinical test used to assess the presence of effusion in the knee joint.
questions.answer_explanation: The patellar tap test is true because it effectively evaluates the presence of excess fluid in the knee joint by detecting the sensation of the patella moving against the underlying structures when tapped, indicating an effusion.

questions.stem_text:
Discuss the impact of the emergent Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) coronavirus on
global health, including its transmission, mortality rate, and public health responses.
questions.gold_answer:
The emergence of the Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) coronavirus has significantly
impacted global health due to its transmission dynamics, high mortality rate, and the
public health responses it necessitated. MERS is primarily transmitted through direct
contact with infected camels or through close human-to-human interaction, which
complicates containment efforts. The mortality rate for MERS has been alarmingly high,
estimated at around 34%, leading to heightened concerns among health authorities
worldwide. In response, global health organizations, including the World Health
Organization, have implemented surveillance measures, enhanced diagnostic capabilities,
and promoted public awareness campaigns to mitigate the spread. These efforts underscore
the importance of strengthening public health infrastructure to respond effectively to
emerging infectious diseases.
questions.answer_explanation: correct because it accurately identifies MERS's unique transmission methods, its significantly high mortality rate, and the resulting public health responses required to manage its spread, all of which are critical factors in assessing its impact on global health.

questions.stem_text:
Discuss the genetic basis of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G 6 PD) deficiency,
focusing on its pattern of inheritance and implications for affected individuals and
populations.
questions.gold_answer:
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G 6 PD) deficiency is primarily inherited in an
X-linked recessive pattern, which means that the gene responsible for this enzyme
deficiency is located on the X chromosome. As a result, males, who have only one X
chromosome, are more severely affected by the deficiency, often presenting with hemolytic
anemia when exposed to certain oxidative stressors. Females, possessing two X chromosomes,
may be carriers and display milder symptoms or none at all, owing to X-inactivation. This
genetic pattern has significant implications for affected populations, particularly in
areas where malaria is prevalent, as G 6 PD deficiency confers some protection against
severe malaria. Understanding the inheritance and population dynamics of G 6 PD deficiency
is crucial for public health strategies and genetic counseling.
questions.answer_explanation: The answer correctly identifies the X-linked recessive inheritance pattern of G6PD deficiency, explaining its greater impact on males due to their single X chromosome and the potential for females to be carriers with milder or no symptoms, which highlights the genetic basis and implications for affected individuals and populations.
